title: Roster proof: Even-key census
topics: Greedy choices, dynamic programming and backtracking
summary: There are n desks and n clerks. readings[row] is an n-bit permission mask for desk row. Assign one distinct clerk to each desk, using only allowed bits. For each possible clerk at desk 0, produce the number of complete assignments with that first clerk; forbidden first choices contribute 0. An empty roster produces no counts. Return how many values in the derived sequence are even, including 0 and negative even values.
descriptionMd:
Permission masks list which clerks may occupy each desk on the day's assignment roster. Alma separates readings for the office's even-numbered keys. A zero reading belongs in that count, just like any other even number.

There are n desks and n clerks. readings[row] is an n-bit permission mask for desk row. Assign one distinct clerk to each desk, using only allowed bits. For each possible clerk at desk 0, produce the number of complete assignments with that first clerk; forbidden first choices contribute 0. An empty roster produces no counts.

Return how many values in the derived sequence are even, including 0 and negative even values.

Implement rosterProofEvenKeyCensus(readings, k). k is part of the common inspection-card signature and does not affect this task's result.
unitIntro: Backtracking with occupancy. There are n desks and n clerks. readings[row] is an n-bit permission mask for desk row. Assign one distinct clerk to each desk, using only allowed bits. For each possible clerk at desk 0, produce the number of complete assignments with that first clerk; forbidden first choices contribute 0. An empty roster produces no counts. Keep the sequence order specified here before computing the requested receipt. A scan invariant says what has been processed and what remains. Work through the proof strip first, then change the returned summary without changing the definition of that sequence. The last card revisits loop accumulators from Hello, Keys.
constraints: 1 <= k <= 8. All arithmetic results fit a signed 32-bit integer.
There are at most 6 desks. Every mask is between 0 and (1 << n) - 1.

Target time O(n*n!); auxiliary space including the derived sequence O(n). n is the input length; d distinct values; q query count; M maximum reading; V vertices; E edges; h tree height; r reported tree nodes.
hints: Start with backtracking with occupancy. What state describes the portion you have already processed?
